questions.stem: What is the general formula for alkanes?
questions.explanation: The general formula for alkanes is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, where n is the number of carbon atoms. For example, methane (n=1) is CH₄ and ethane (n=2) is C₂H₆.

questions.stem: What type of bonds are found between carbon atoms in alkanes?
questions.explanation: Alkanes contain only single covalent bonds between carbon atoms. This makes them saturated hydrocarbons -- they cannot accept any more hydrogen atoms.

questions.stem: What are the complete combustion products of an alkane?
questions.explanation: When alkanes undergo complete combustion (burning in excess oxygen), they produce carbon dioxide and water: hydrocarbon + oxygen → CO₂ + H₂O.

questions.stem: What is the molecular formula of propane?
questions.explanation: Propane has 3 carbon atoms (n=3). Using CₙH₂ₙ₊₂: C₃H₂₍₃₎₊₂ = C₃H₈.

questions.stem: Why are alkanes described as 'saturated' hydrocarbons?

options.text: Because they are dissolved in water
Because they contain only single bonds, with the maximum number of hydrogen atoms

questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated because all carbon-carbon bonds are single bonds. Each carbon atom bonds to the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms, so no more can be added.

questions.stem: What happens during incomplete combustion of alkanes?

options.text: Carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot) may be produced instead of carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: In a limited supply of oxygen, incomplete combustion occurs. This produces carbon monoxide (a toxic gas) and/or carbon (soot) instead of carbon dioxide, plus water.

questions.stem: Why are alkanes generally unreactive apart from combustion?

options.text: Their C-C and C-H single bonds are strong and difficult to break
They are too large to react

questions.explanation: Alkanes are relatively unreactive because the C-C and C-H single bonds are strong and non-polar. There is no functional group or reactive site for other molecules to attack easily.
